doc: SELECT *, | FROM dbo.Customers
note: column completion after star plus comma stays scoped to Customers

doc: SELECT * FROM |
note: FROM position after SELECT * offers tables, not columns

doc: SELECT c.| FROM dbo.Customers c
note: alias-dot in select list scoped to Customers columns only

doc: SELECT o.*, c.| FROM dbo.Orders o JOIN dbo.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
note: after o.* the c. qualifier must still scope to Customers, not the star's table

doc: SELECT TOP (10) | FROM dbo.Products
note: column completion works right after TOP (n)

doc: SELECT DISTINCT | FROM dbo.Customers
note: column completion works right after DISTINCT

doc: select distinct Cou| from dbo.Customers
note: lowercase keywords with 3-char prefix after DISTINCT filters to Country

doc: SELECT TOP 5 e.| FROM dbo.Employees e
note: unparenthesized TOP followed by alias-dot scoped to Employees

doc:
SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName
FROM dbo.Customers
UNION
SELECT o.| FROM dbo.Orders o
note: UNION second branch alias scopes to Orders, first-branch Customers columns must not leak

doc: SELECT ProductID FROM dbo.Products UNION ALL SELECT | FROM dbo.OrderDetails
note: UNION ALL second branch bare select list scoped to OrderDetails only

doc: SELECT OrderID FROM dbo.Orders UNION SELECT InvoiceID FROM |
note: FROM position in UNION second branch offers tables, not columns

doc: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM dbo.Customers c UNION SELECT x.| FROM dbo.Orders x
note: second-branch alias x binds to Orders; first-branch c/Customers must not bleed in

doc:
SELECT * FROM dbo.Products;
SELECT | FROM dbo.Customers
note: prior semicolon-terminated star statement must not leak Products columns into next statement

doc:
SELECT p.ProductID, p.Price FROM dbo.Products p;
SELECT cust.| FROM dbo.Customers cust
note: long alias in second statement scoped to Customers; earlier statement's Products columns absent

doc:
SELECT o.OrderID FROM dbo.Orders o;
SELECT o.| FROM dbo.OrderDetails o
note: alias o redefined after semicolon must rebind to OrderDetails, not stale Orders

doc: SELECT TOP (5) * FROM |
note: FROM after TOP (n) star offers tables and views

doc: Select Distinct s.| From dbo.Suppliers s
note: mixed-case keywords; DISTINCT alias-dot scoped to Suppliers

doc: SELECT sh.| FROM dbo.Shippers sh
note: two-char alias scoped to Shippers; similarly-named Suppliers columns absent

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Orders WHERE |
note: WHERE after SELECT * still resolves Orders columns

doc: SELECT c.* FROM dbo.Customers c JOIN dbo.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.|
note: c.* projection does not affect o. scoping in WHERE

doc:
SELECT TOP (25)
    p.ProductName,
    p.|
FROM dbo.Products p
note: multi-line TOP select list, alias-dot on continuation line

doc: SELECT *, C| FROM dbo.Customers
note: 1-char prefix after star+comma filters Customers columns to C-names

doc: SELECT DISTINCT TOP (10) | FROM dbo.Orders
note: combined DISTINCT TOP still yields Orders column completion

doc: SELECT i.*, | FROM Sales.Invoices i
note: bare column position after alias.* scoped to Sales.Invoices

doc: SELECT CustomerID FROM dbo.vw_CustomerOrders UNION SELECT | FROM dbo.Customers
note: view in first branch must not leak its extra columns into Customers-scoped second branch

doc: SELECT v.| FROM dbo.vw_ProductCatalog v
note: view alias exposes only view columns, not base Products columns

doc:
SELECT Phone FROM dbo.Shippers
UNION
SELECT Phone FROM dbo.Suppliers
UNION
SELECT | FROM dbo.Customers
note: third UNION branch scoped to Customers; earlier branches' tables must not leak

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Products ORDER BY |
note: ORDER BY after SELECT * resolves Products columns

doc: SELECT ord.| FROM dbo.Orders AS ord
note: AS-introduced alias resolves to Orders columns

doc:
EXEC dbo.usp_UpdateProductPrice @ProductID = 1, @NewPrice = 9.99;
SELECT | FROM dbo.Products
note: prior EXEC statement's parameters must not appear in the next SELECT list

doc: select top (3) c.co| from dbo.Customers c
note: lowercase 2-char prefix after alias-dot matches case-insensitively

doc: SELECT d.| FROM (SELECT OrderID, OrderDate FROM dbo.Orders) d
note: derived table exposes only projected columns, not the rest of Orders

doc: SELECT * FROM (SELECT ProductID, ProductName FROM dbo.Products) AS d WHERE d.|
note: outer SELECT * with derived table: WHERE d. limited to derived projection

doc:
SELECT
    o.OrderID,
    o.*,
    |
FROM dbo.Orders o
JOIN dbo.Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipperID
note: multi-line select list mixing explicit column, alias.*, then bare position over a 2-table join

doc: SELECT City FROM dbo.Customers UNION SELECT Ci| FROM dbo.Suppliers
note: prefix filtering inside UNION second branch scoped to Suppliers

doc: SELECT TOP (10) p.Price * 2 AS DoublePrice, p.| FROM dbo.Products p
note: alias-dot after an expression with AS alias still scoped to Products

doc:
SELECT SupplierID FROM dbo.Suppliers;
SELECT EmployeeID FROM dbo.Employees UNION SELECT | FROM dbo.Orders
note: prior statement plus UNION: last branch scoped to Orders only

doc: SELECT DISTINCT o.| FROM dbo.Orders o WHERE o.OrderDate > '2024-01-01'
note: DISTINCT with alias-dot and trailing WHERE clause resolves Orders columns

doc:
SELECT * FROM dbo.Categories;
SELECT TOP (5) | FROM dbo.Categories
note: TOP position in a fresh statement after a semicolon-terminated star query

doc: SELECT TOP (100) * FROM dbo.vw_CustomerOrders WHERE |
note: TOP star over a view: WHERE offers view columns, not base-table extras
